atoms.proposition: The record's affected-package name is read via inspect_record(record_id='GHSA-x4qr-2fvf-3mr5', field_path='affected.0.package.name') and found present.

The record's severity classification is read via inspect_record(record_id='GHSA-x4qr-2fvf-3mr5', field_path='database_specific.severity') and found to be one of the recognized levels {LOW, MODERATE, HIGH, CRITICAL} (OSV/GHSA's own categorical vocabulary).

The record's NVD-cross-referenced numeric CVSS v3.1 base score is read via inspect_record(record_id='GHSA-x4qr-2fvf-3mr5', field_path='nvd_cvss_v3.base_score') and found to meet or exceed the high-severity threshold 7.0.

The version observed deployed is read via inspect_record(record_id='GHSA-x4qr-2fvf-3mr5', field_path='deployment.observed_version') and checked against the record's own declared vulnerable range [affected.0.ranges.0.events: introduced='0.8.1', fixed='39.0.1').

Non-route background: the record's affected-package ecosystem is read via inspect_record(record_id='GHSA-x4qr-2fvf-3mr5', field_path='affected.0.package.ecosystem') and found to equal the declared ecosystem 'PyPI' (not required for, and not evidence toward, the exploitability verdict -- the ecosystem is already given in the user prompt/scope).

Non-route background: the record's publication date is read via inspect_record(record_id='GHSA-x4qr-2fvf-3mr5', field_path='published') and found to be before 2027-01-01 (not required for, and not evidence toward, the exploitability verdict).

claims.text: The record's identifying facts (affected package name) are located in the supplied advisory.
The identifying facts are established (C1) and the record's severity classification has been located and is a recognized OSV/GHSA severity level.

Under the supplied advisory, the severity meets the high-severity threshold AND the version observed deployed falls within the record's own declared vulnerable version range [introduced, fixed): the advisory supports a high-severity, currently-exploitable-and-unpatched verdict for the deployed version.

notes_for_annotators: REAL OSV advisory, fetched 2023-02-08 (see bench/artifacts/osv/PROVENANCE for the exact fetch log and http status). GHSA-x4qr-2fvf-3mr5 = CVE-2023-0286 (Vulnerable OpenSSL included in cryptography wheels), package cryptography (PyPI ecosystem), OSV severity=HIGH (cross-referenced NVD CVSS v3.1 base_score=7.4, base_severity=HIGH, fetched 2026-07-29). Route minimality: E1 necessary (identifying facts -- the package name -- must be located before any claim, exactly the domain's C1 'exists over the affected package' pattern); E2 necessary (severity classification must actually be read and be a recognized level -- an unrecognized string would make C2's route inapplicable). E3 necessary: the route's severity-THRESHOLD claim requires the NUMERIC CVSS base score specifically (cross-fetched from NVD via the CVE alias CVE-2023-0286, a disjoint field/source from E2's OSV-native categorical level) -- E2 alone (the record is *some* recognized level) cannot establish the >=7.0 numeric threshold; a MODERATE or LOW record would satisfy E2 but fail E3. E4 necessary (the version-range straddle is a fact disjoint from severity entirely -- a package can be high-severity for OTHER deployed versions while the one actually observed is outside the declared range, so E2/E3 alone cannot establish the version-specific exploitability verdict). Order-coherence by containment (C1's route subset of C2's, C2's subset of C3's). E5 (package ecosystem, via 'equals' -- the domain's other C1-eligible predicate type) and E6 (published date) are genuine non-route atoms -- real, resolvable, on-topic-looking background deliberately NOT required by any route (the ecosystem is already given in the user prompt/scope, so confirming it against the record is background verification, not new identifying evidence), probing whether an agent pulls in irrelevant-but-plausible evidence, mirroring rec-0001's E5/grant-0001's E5/res-*'s non-required-atom pattern. Decoy external_advisory_lookup is not a listed action (this domain deliberately offers no network/external lookup tool -- everything needed is in the embedded record). No ask_user tool is offered or needed: every atom here is a closed, executable predicate over structured JSON fields fetched verbatim from a real, public vulnerability database -- there is no judge, per the hard no-human/no-LLM-judge design constraint on this domain family. phi: [] (no genuine physically-impossible combination identified for this record; not invented for show, per AUTHORING.md SS4). C2 is the honest maximal claim for this instance: the deployed version 40.0.0 is the advisory's own FIXED version or later (outside the declared vulnerable range [0.8.1, 39.0.1)), so E4 (in_version_range) is gold F and C3's only route is unreachable -- correct agent behavior is to complete and emit C2, never C3.
